title: PHD: Parallel Huffman Decoder on FPGA for Extreme Performance and Energy Efficiency
problem: Huffman decoding requires efficient management of fine-grained parallelism with inter-codeword dependencies on memory-constrained FPGAs while exploiting subsequence-level parallelism.
motivation: Huffman decoding is crucial for data compression and requires efficient hardware acceleration to achieve extreme performance and energy efficiency.
method: PHD implements self-synchronization-based parallel Huffman decoding on FPGA using bit-level, subsequence-level, and tile-level parallelism. It employs a hybrid memory architecture to efficiently store the codebook and introduces the ONCE MORE optimization to reduce decoding loop iterations while managing inter-codeword dependencies.
key_novelty: First FPGA accelerator for self-synchronization-based parallel Huffman decoding that combines multiple granularities of parallelism with hybrid memory and optimization techniques.
contributions: First self-synchronization-based parallel Huffman decoder on FPGA
Multi-level parallelism design spanning bit-level, subsequence-level, and tile-level granularities
Hybrid memory system for efficient codebook storage addressing on-chip memory constraints
ONCE MORE optimization to reduce decoding loop iterations
primary_theme: Efficient FPGA acceleration of parallel Huffman decoding
